pages.text: Nothing here is crafted at a bench. Everything is made by holding two things and pressing $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact) - and most of it has to be $(l)thought of$() first, or your hands go through the motions and sometimes ruin the material.

$(l)Any stage$()$(li)Nesting material + nesting material = a nest$(br2)$(l)Habilis$()$(li)Stick or sharpened stick + flake = pointy stick$(li)Long branch + flake = sharpened spear$(li)Rock + flake = chopper$(li)Long branch + chopper = digging stick

$(l)Erectus$()$(li)Long branch + rock = wooden club$(li)Sharpened spear, right-clicked on a fire four times (or held there) = fire-hardened spear$(br2)A grinding rock, held against a blunted edge, puts the edge back.
Two loose cobbles knock together into this. It is the tool that opens every other one.

$(l)Knapping$() is its own screen: hold a rock with a hammerstone in your off hand and press $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact). It offers what you could try to strike off - a flake, a chopper, a multi tool - and good stone breaks better than bad.$(br2)A multi tool takes 8 chert, 10 basalt, 2 obsidian or a chert hammerstone.

$(l)What the stone is worth$()$(li)Chert - the finest edge, the rarest find$(li)Basalt - a tier behind chert, and always near lava$(li)Quartzite - coarse, plentiful, dependable$(li)Obsidian - sharper than anything, and only up high$(li)Limestone - will not hold an edge. Good for grinding, nothing else.
